title: THE WOODLAND TRAIL
subtitle: Training simulation 02
summary: Rain fell overnight and stopped an hour ago. Several items are wet, and wet evidence spoils quickly in the wrong packaging.
objective: Collect every item. Ask yourself whether each one is wet or dry before you choose a container.

background.alt: A woodland path after rain, with conifers, a fallen log, and a puddle

evidence.name: Shoe impression cast
evidence.alt: A plaster cast of a shoe sole with tread ridges
evidence.description: A plaster cast lifted from a deep shoe impression in the soft mud of the trail.
evidence.success: The rigid box supports the cast so its tread detail cannot snap or crumble.
evidence.failure: Unsupported, the cast cracked in transit and the tread pattern can no longer be compared.

evidence.name: Torn cloth scrap
evidence.alt: A torn scrap of blue cloth with water droplets
evidence.description: A rain-soaked scrap of blue cloth snagged on a low branch beside the path.
evidence.success: Paper lets the soaked cloth dry out slowly instead of stewing in its own moisture.
evidence.failure: Sealed while wet, the cloth stayed damp and mildew spread across the fibres.

evidence.name: Glass bottle
evidence.description: A dry glass bottle lying against the fallen log, possibly handled without gloves.
evidence.success: The rigid container stops the glass knocking about, so the bottle and its fingerprints survive.
evidence.failure: The bottle cracked against something hard in transit, taking the fingerprint ridges with it.

evidence.name: Cigarette butt
evidence.alt: A cigarette butt with a tan filter
evidence.description: A damp cigarette butt at the edge of the puddle. The filter may carry saliva.
evidence.success: The damp filter dries safely, so the saliva sample stays usable for DNA work.
evidence.failure: Moisture sealed in with the filter let bacteria multiply and break the DNA down.

evidence.name: Leather glove
evidence.description: A soaked leather glove dropped in the undergrowth, well off the path.
evidence.success: Breathable paper draws the water out of the leather without cooking the evidence inside it.
evidence.failure: The wet leather sweated inside its seal and rotted, along with any skin cells in the lining.

evidence.name: Set of keys
evidence.alt: Two keys on a split ring
evidence.description: A dry set of keys half buried in leaf litter at the foot of a tree.
evidence.success: The sealed bag keeps the keys and the leaf debris clinging to them together and dry.
evidence.failure: The keys were not sealed in, so loose debris and any trace on it went missing.

evidence.name: Crumpled receipt
evidence.description: A dry crumpled receipt caught under a stone. The print is still readable.
evidence.success: Sealed away from the weather, the ink stays readable and the paper keeps its shape.
evidence.failure: Left open to the damp air, the paper softened and the printed detail blurred.

evidence.name: Hair clip
evidence.description: A dry plastic hair clip in the undergrowth, with several hairs still caught in it.
evidence.success: The seal holds the clip and the hairs caught in it in one place.
evidence.failure: The hairs worked loose from the clip and were lost before the item reached the lab.
